text:
liz: anyone else seeing a sudden p99 spike in eu-west GPU queues?
omar: yep, started ~09:12. NVLink errors + KV cache churn in telemetry
devon: which tenant? noisy neighbor or batch spill?
liz: tenant-omega kicked off a heavy rerank job at 09:10, aligns with spike
sasha: can we soft-isolate them to a dedicated slice while investigating? costs must be checked
omar: dedicated fallback available but only 2 slots free in eu-west. If we carve them out we blow preemptible capacity
devon: short term: limit tenant-omega burst via router policy (burst_limit -> 60rps) and throttle prefix cache regen
liz: oncall, can you flip a test throttle for tenant-omega in staging then mirror to prod canary?
oncall: I can trigger a canary change. command: `POST /router/policies -d '{"tenant":"tenant-omega","burst_limit":60}'`
infra-bot: policy-change request received; running canary in us-west first
omar: watch nvlink CRC errs. If those go down, it's probably noisy neighbor, not infra fabric
sasha: if we move them to dedicated, estimate +$2.8k/day for the reserved slice (short lived). tradeoff: better p99 now vs cost
liz: agreed. let's try router throttle first, measure 15m after canary
devon: also add telemetry flag to emit TensorLoad/kvcache churn for that tenant, helps root cause
sasha: opening ticket INFRA-1029 with rollback plan and SLA impact notes
sasha: ticket INFRA-1029 created: "tenant-omega rerank -> p99 tail, temporary throttle + dedicated fallback plan"
omar: can someone run a quick kstat on affected nodes? `kubectl logs node-gpu-23 | grep -i nvlink`
oncall: grabbed logs, sending snippet:
```
[kernel] nvlink: link 2 CRC errors increased 43 -> 129
[serving] kvcache regen spikes: 1200 ops/s -> 5400 ops/s
```
liz: thanks. that lines up with aggressive KV cache churn from large batch completions
devon: plan: 1) canary throttle now 2) monitor 15m 3) if still bad, failover tenant to dedicated slice with preemptible eviction guard 4) analyze model batch sizing
sasha: noted. assigning owners: throttle=oncall, failover=omar, postmortem=devon
oncall: canary throttle applied to us-west at 09:24, will mirror to eu-west in 2m if stable
infra-bot: canary health check: us-west p99 -> 210ms (was 820ms). no regressions observed
liz: great signal. mirror to eu-west now please
oncall: mirrored to eu-west at 09:27
omar: eu-west p99 dropped to 240ms, nvlink errs stabilized
sasha: cost update: if we need dedicated fallback it'll be active ~4-6 hours, est cost +$600-$900 for the window
devon: let's avoid dedicated unless throttle fails. also capture a sample set of requests for evals to see if throttling impacts quality
liz: creating a quick dashboard slice for tenant-omega tail latencies + nvlink errs
sasha: added automation: if nvlink CRC errors >100 in 15m, trigger alert and auto-throttle
oncall: monitoring live. will post when 30m window complete
liz: thanks team. follow-up: devon will run root-cause analysis, sasha will log cost impact, omar will prepare fallback script
omar: fallback script ready in `infra/scripts/fallback_pin.sh`, we just need an approved runbook
devon: will draft runbook and link to INFRA-1029
sasha: INFRA-1029 updated with runbook link
liz: good. thumbs up if no objections :thumbsup:
omar: :thumbsup:
oncall: :thumbsup:
devon: :thumbsup:
infra-bot: incident-preventive-checklist: KV cache tuning, burst limits, dedicated-fallback reviewed"
